content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias after sharp price spikes (e.g., 48.12, 49.30, 51.55) — model overshoots and fails to correct downward.
- Model underestimates sharp downward corrections (e.g., 48.37 → 37.27, 44.49 → 34.33) — fails to recognize mean reversion or volatility drops.
- Forecast trend often lags true price movements — model reacts slowly to sudden drops or spikes.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the second half of the 30d forecast (e.g., 42.00–42.60 vs true 41.16–42.61), suggesting overconfidence in upward continuation.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or event-driven volatility — e.g., 34.33 drop after 45.93 peak is not captured.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent history — model ignores recent low prices (e.g., 33.70, 33.16) when forecasting upward trends.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp reversals or sudden drops in price (e.g., 45.93 → 34.33, 44.49 → 33.16).
